_why: RUSSIAN IS THE DECK WHERE THE OBVIOUS TARGETS ARE THE WRONG ONES. Russian inside Russia is heavily standardised, so Moscow, Petersburg, Novosibirsk and Yekaterinburg are barely separable by ear and would make five rounds of the same answer. check-decks.mjs records the rule this deck actually runs on: the old 'native or official language' test admitted standard Minsk Russian, barely separable from Moscow, while excluding Armenian and Georgian Russian where non-Slavic substrate makes the variety MORE recognisable. So the deck is built on the post-Soviet spread, where each Russian-speaking community carries a different substrate: Turkic in Bishkek and Tashkent, Romanian in Chisinau, Finnic in Tallinn, Baltic in Riga, Hebrew in Haifa. Already held: Yerevan, Tbilisi, Odesa, Almaty, Moscow.
